correctness.rationale: The proof gives an exact finite reduction.  Every degree-two target is uniquely \(z=2q\) with \(q\in\{-1,0,1\}^{15}\), feasibility is exactly the sixteen Sylvester inequalities, and every source-lattice summand is a feasible sign vector. The carry-free base-three encoding turns decomposition into exact pair-sum membership.  The packaged verifier exhausts all \(2^{15}\) sign vectors and all \(3^{15}\) ternary targets, obtaining 9552 source points, 6350363 feasible targets, 6215123 decomposable targets, and hence 135240 holes.  The \(\operatorname{AGL}(4,2)\) action is checked algebraically and its generated orbit partition has the five claimed sizes summing to the full hole count.  No finite sample is used to infer an infinite statement. The resulting orbit sizes are \(840,13440,26880,40320,53760\), and they sum to \(135240\).

originality.rationale: The closest primary source, arXiv:2609.32950v1, proves that the identical \(P_{5,1}\) is integral and nonnormal and displays one degree-two hole, but does not count all degree-two holes or classify their natural affine-character symmetry orbits. Santos 2007 gives a different lower-region obstruction and asks for the normality range of the truncations. published-finding corpus and web searches using object, hole, Hilbert-basis, decomposition, numeric, and symmetry aliases found no covering statement. The final checked claim is the exact cardinality \(|H_2|=135240\) together with natural \(\operatorname{AGL}(4,2)\) orbit sizes \(840,13440,26880,40320,53760\).

value.rationale: This is a natural complete finite invariant of the lead source's first explicit integral-but-nonnormal Sylvester threshold example.  It upgrades a single obstruction witness to the entire degree-two obstruction set and reduces 135240 holes to five symmetry types, which is useful for subsequent semigroup and Hilbert-basis analysis.  The slice is not arbitrary: degree two is the first degree in which the source already proves normality fails.  The result does not claim higher-degree consequences. The five natural symmetry-orbit sizes are \(840,13440,26880,40320,53760\).
